name: Lake Istokpoga
type: Shallow (10 ft at most): bulrush, cattails, pads, Kissimmee grass and islands
pool: Deepest spot about 10 ft;Canal gates on the south end move water and fish
notes: Spawn under way. Bass bed on the full and new moons; specks in the pads.
Peak spawn for big bass. Fish the moons and the calm days.
Late spawners and the first post-spawn fish.
Post-spawn. Shellcracker spawn on the full moon.
Shad spawn at dawn; bluegill bed on the full moon.
Summer pattern: topwater early, then mats and offshore grass.
Hottest stretch. Fish first light, last light and after storms.
Hottest water. Short bites at dawn and around storms.
Shad move shallow as the nights cool.
Fall feed. Bass school on shad around the grass.
Pre-spawn starts; specks school in open water as fronts arrive.
Pre-spawn. Bass stage on outside grass; first beds on warm spells.

flbass.doing: Cold fronts push bass to the outside grass lines and the deepest holes. Between fronts they slide toward the spawning flats, and the biggest fish of the year start to move.
how: Lipless crankbait or jerkbait over sparse hydrilla and eelgrass; slow it down after a front.
Punch mats with a 1 to 1.5 oz tungsten weight, or a slow Texas rig on the first hard edge.
Wild shiner under a float beside reed clumps and on outside grass: the trophy season.

specks.doing: Specks school in open water over the deepest flats, channels and offshore grass, suspended at a different depth from day to day.
how: Missouri minnows or grass shrimp, or spider-rig small jigs (hair jigs, tubes, Hal Flies).
Set minnows at several depths, then match the one that bites.
Cast a small jig to schools you see on forward-facing sonar.

bream.doing: Slow. Bluegill and shellcracker hold in deeper grass, canals and around docks; warm, sunny afternoons bring them up.
how: Grass shrimp on the bottom next to hydrilla or eelgrass.
Small jig or worm along canal edges and docks.

flbass.doing: Late fall and early winter are the best time for big bass on live wild shiners, as the cooling water picks up the bite.
how: Wild shiners along reed lines and island grass.
Lipless crankbait or spinnerbait on wind-swept points and creek mouths.

specks.doing: Winter is speck season. Drift open water in the northeast and southwest corners (the southwest holds the deepest water, about 10 ft), deeper cuts around the islands and the outer edge of the spatterdock.
how: Live Missouri minnows or grass shrimp.
Napier deer hair jigs, tube jigs or Hal Flies for schooling fish.
Move until you find concentrated fish.

bream.doing: Shellcracker move onto firm sand and shell near the grass ahead of the spring full moons; bluegill feed around reeds and docks.
how: Red wigglers on the bottom with a split shot.
Crickets or grass shrimp under a small float along reeds.

flbass.doing: Bass spawn from mid to late January, often near bulrush, cattails and lily pads on the north and west shores and around Big and Bumblebee islands.
how: Soft plastics or a weightless speed worm.
Swimbait along the outside of the spawning grass.

specks.doing: Specks spawn over sandy bottom near bulrush and cattails. Henderson's Cove, the north end, pad and grass edges near deeper water, and open water around Big Island and the west shore of Long Island all produce.
how: Minnows or grass shrimp under a cork over sand by the reeds.
Small jigs and spinners between the spawning areas.

bream.doing: Shellcracker bed on the March and April full moons on firm sand and shell near grass. Bluegill start as the water warms.
how: Red wigglers on the bottom; work the area until you find the colony.
Small beetle spin along the edge of the flat.

flbass.doing: After the spawn, bass hold in the bulrush and cattails and on eelgrass and hydrilla.
how: Soft plastics into bulrush and cattail.
Spinnerbait, spoon or jerkbait around eelgrass or hydrilla.

specks.doing: After the spawn, specks scatter to deeper grass edges, docks, bridges and channel edges. The bite slows as the water warms.
how: Minnows at dock pilings, bridges and fish attractors.
Small jig swum along the deep edge of the vegetation.

bream.doing: Bluegill and redear here often approach a pound. Late spring through summer is best, in dense bulrush, Kissimmee grass, cattails and pads.
how: Crickets or grass shrimp under a cork.
Try the cypress on the southeast side.

flbass.doing: Bass stay around the islands and their grass all year. When the gates are open, water moving into the Istokpoga Canal turns on the south end and the canal itself.
how: Plastic worms and lizards in junebug or red shad.
Lipless crankbait at the Arbuckle and Josephine creek mouths when they flow.
The canal off CR 621 is good bank fishing when the gates are open.

specks.doing: The slowest season. Specks suspend in the deepest water, on fish attractors and in shade; fish early, late or at night.
how: Lights and minnows at bridges and deep docks.
Vertical jig or minnow at the depth you mark.

bream.doing: Bluegill keep spawning on each full moon; between moons they hold in deeper pads, grass patches and around docks. Fish early.
how: Grass shrimp in deep pads and hydrilla patches; anchor and chum lightly.
Worms and crickets along the walkways.

flbass.doing: Cooling water picks up the bass bite. Fish wind-swept points in the grass and creek mouths when water is moving.
how: Worms and lizards in junebug or red shad.
Live wild shiners for the bigger fish.

specks.doing: The speck bite is slow until the water cools, then picks up in open water.
how: Missouri minnows under a cork, or trolled small jigs and spinners.

bream.doing: Bream feed hard in the grass as the water cools. Fewer beds, steady numbers.
how: Anchor near a thick hydrilla patch and fish grass shrimp or worms near the bottom.
Crickets under a cork along reed lines.

zones.name: South end and the canal

zones.name: East-shore reed lines
zones.t: Bulrush lines for worms and shiners.

zones.name: Southwest corner
zones.t: Deepest water in the lake, about 10 ft.

zones.name: Big Island and Long Island
zones.t: Open water and pad edges near the islands.

zones.name: Bulrush, grass and pads
zones.t: Dense cover on the west and north shores.
